title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1969-04-05
lineage: SBD > Rm (7 inch Master Reels @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) > DAT > Sonic Solutions > CD > EAC > Samplitude > SHN

ai_review.summary: Pristine soundboard capture of the Avalon Ballroom ’69 set, highlighted by a soaring Dark Star and the Mountains‑of‑the‑Moon → Dark Star segue.
ai_review.review: This Charlie Miller‑sourced recording delivers crystal‑clear, tape‑warm sound that lets the 1969 Avalon performance shine. The show is a psychedelic high point – stellar Dark Star, an inspired Mountains of the Moon/Dark Star transition, ripping Alligator and a fluid Eleven/Feedback sequence – with only the early Hard To Handle stumbling out of sync. Overall it’s regarded as one of the band’s top ’69 outings.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 50 reviews, the vast majority are 5‑star and praise both performance and audio; only a handful note minor flaws (hiss, one weak song). Weighted toward show quality, the consensus yields an excellent rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean tape sound with a faint vintage hiss typical of ’69 tapes; no drop‑outs or major mix problems. Charlie Miller’s transfer is repeatedly called ‘pristine’ and “clean quality”.

standout_songs: Mountains of the Moon → Dark Star
show_quality.setlist_flow: A psychedelic arc that opens acoustic (Duprees, Mountains) and flips electric into a sprawling Dark Star, then rockets through an adventurous second set with unusual segues (Eleven → Lovelight → Eleven) and tight jams that keep the momentum high despite occasional rough spots.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work is repeatedly called ‘on fire’, with a perfect tone on Dark Star, aggressive solos, slide work on Hard To Handle, and expressive acoustic playing on Duprees/Mountains.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh gets strong mentions for his bass driving the Star medley, solid form throughout, and “six‑armed” interplay with the drummers.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir is noted for early vocal cracks and a developing style; occasional criticism of his voice on Hard To Handle but generally part of the evolving sound.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s piano on Duprees is likened to a carousel, and keyboards are praised in the overall mix (no specific mention of Keith or Brent).
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart are described as a single creature with “six arms”, delivering tight, flowing rhythms and powerful transitions.
